decision: replace the rate mark stack with per-request eth accrual on the redeem request
why: the claim path walk, the positional floor and the carry side-car all exist only because pricing is lazy and positional

decision: checked whether the rate mark work is deployed anywhere before planning storage changes
why: widening the anchor mapping changes its stride and would garble every existing entry
result: nothing past 1.2.1 is live, so layout is free

decision: one uint on the anchor is not enough, the claim path needs credited eth and credited lsETH
why: a single global cursor reads a settled gap as credited and caps that span at zero payout
result: corrected the design before any code

decision: pro rata on the new counter is wrong, the formula has to be additive
why: credited eth covers a prefix, not the whole request, so dividing it across the full amount underpays
result: replaced with an additive cap, checked by hand against 4 pinned tests

decision: point 4 triggers on settlement, not on rebalancing
why: the redeem manager cannot see the funding source, reportWithdraw gets one mixed lump
result: avoided a zero payout path that loses user funds

decision: corrected the dos cost estimate down by about fifty times, from 100k requests to about 2k
why: at roughly 31k gas per covered request a 60M gas report covers about 2000, not 100000
result: user kept the loop unbounded, so the ceiling gets measured in ci instead

decision: recorded what every request is paid across 200 seeded scenarios before changing anything
why: wanted the check to read as old number against new number per request, not as an argument about equivalence

decision: put a proxy per scenario over one shared implementation instead of redeploying the implementation
why: 200 implementation deploys alone overran forge's 2^30 test gas limit

decision: deliberately broke the settledHeight clamp to check the baseline would notice
why: a gate nobody has seen fail is not a gate
evidence: diff of 361 of 1501 rows, both directions
result: gate is sensitive, mutation reverted and baseline reproduced byte identical

decision: noted the conservation and non-zero-payout invariants both passed under that mutation
why: they catch eth being created or lost, not eth going to the wrong redeemer
result: baseline diff is the load-bearing gate, invariants are a second net
